headline: Stocks Look to Steady After Lopsided Selloff as Gulf Tensions Linger
body_html:
U.S. stocks look to open Wednesday trying to steady themselves after a lopsided Tuesday session. Of the 664 names in our universe, only 143 rose while 519 fell. Financials took the heaviest hit, down 5.14%, with software off 2.88% and homebuilders down 1.91%. Semiconductors were the lone group in the green, up 0.23%.

The overnight news flow is dominated by geopolitics. Reports say Iran struck US bases in Gulf countries even as diplomacy continues, and a US official said American forces hit an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island. Separately, a crew member is missing after an attack on a UAE-owned vessel near Hormuz. Oil, though, eased as higher US crude stockpiles tempered supply worries.

At the open, watch whether chip strength holds with a major chipmaker's results looming and the Anthropic debut drawing attention. Also watch whether the surge in market volatility keeps spreading beyond AI worries. Single-stock swings were large Tuesday: Nextracker fell 12.13% and Salesforce 9.45%, while AECOM jumped 11.08%. Early prices are thin, so judge the tone only after the first hour.

briefs.headline: Financials Post the Day's Deepest Sector Loss
briefs.body: Financials dropped 5.14% on Tuesday, the steepest slide among the nine groups we track and well ahead of software's 2.88% decline. Traders will look at the open for any sign of stabilization, or whether the selling carries into a second day.

briefs.headline: Software Slump Leaves Salesforce Down Nearly 10%
briefs.body: Salesforce lost 9.45% as the software group fell 2.88%. BlackBerry also slid, down 6.96%. With volatility gauges reportedly climbing again, the question at the open is whether buyers step in for beaten-down software names or sellers press further.

briefs.headline: Solar Names Take a Beating
briefs.body: Nextracker was Tuesday's worst performer in our universe, down 12.13%, and Enphase Energy lost 7.58%. Waste Connections also fell sharply, down 8.01%. Solar-linked stocks will be closely watched for follow-through selling or a bounce when trading begins.

briefs.headline: Chips Hold Up While Everything Else Sags
briefs.body: Semiconductors rose 0.23%, the only sector gain on Tuesday. Arm Holdings added 4.76% and Astera Labs 4.58%. Attention now turns to a major chipmaker's coming results, which could decide whether that resilience lasts or fades.

briefs.headline: Oil Slips as US Inventories Build
briefs.body: Crude prices eased after data showed higher US stockpiles, which softened worries about supply. That calm sits uneasily beside reports of fresh attacks in the Gulf, so the open will test whether energy traders keep leaning on inventories or shift toward the security risks.

briefs.headline: Summit Diplomacy Shares the Stage With Gulf Strikes
briefs.body: Xi and Putin criticized sanctions ahead of a planned meeting with Trump in China, while Trump praised ties with the Philippines before those talks. At home, a US Navy chief faced sharp questions at a hearing over the Iran conflict and its toll on sailors.
